cases.name: Crowded teeth
cases.summary: Teeth overlap or sit outside the line of the dental arch.
recognition: Some teeth may also be rotated
review: Assess available space using clinical records
Review hygiene access and gum health
Discuss alignment goals with the patient
cases.limits: A photograph cannot establish root positions, available bone, or a treatment plan.

quiz.question: Which observation most directly describes crowding?
quiz.explanation: Crowding describes tooth alignment and space; root and bone findings require additional assessment.

cases.name: Generalized spacing
cases.summary: Gaps occur between several teeth rather than at one contact.
review: Review gum health and previous tooth loss
Assess tooth size and arch relationships
cases.limits: Gaps have different causes; appearance does not establish the cause or best approach.

quiz.question: What should happen before choosing how to close spaces?
options: Predict treatment time from a selfie
quiz.explanation: Space management depends on the complete dental situation, not the visible gap alone.

cases.name: Midline diastema
cases.summary: A space separates the central front teeth at the dental midline.
review: Record whether the gap is changing
cases.limits: A midline gap may be developmental in mixed dentition; a photo cannot explain its cause.

quiz.question: Is every childhood midline gap a disease?
options: Yes, if no braces are present
quiz.explanation: Mixed-dentition spacing can be developmental and needs context before any treatment decision.

cases.name: Deep bite
cases.summary: The upper front teeth overlap the lower front teeth excessively in the vertical direction.
review: Inspect for palatal or gingival trauma
cases.limits: A frontal image alone cannot quantify overlap or confirm traumatic contact.

quiz.question: Deep bite primarily describes which direction?
quiz.explanation: Deep bite concerns vertical overlap; overjet concerns the horizontal incisor relationship.

cases.name: Anterior open bite
cases.summary: A gap remains between front teeth when the back teeth come together.
cases.limits: An open-mouth photograph is not proof of open bite; confirm the bite position.

quiz.question: Which observation is needed to describe an anterior open bite?
options: Front gap while back teeth meet
quiz.explanation: An anterior gap must be considered with the posterior teeth in confirmed closure.

cases.name: Posterior open bite
cases.summary: One or more back-tooth regions lack vertical contact in the confirmed bite.
recognition: May affect one or both sides
cases.limits: Incomplete eruption and an unclosed mouth must not be labelled automatically as posterior open bite.

quiz.question: Why is a back-tooth gap in one photo insufficient?
quiz.explanation: Clinical bite position and eruption status must be established before interpreting separation.

cases.name: Underbite / reverse overjet
cases.summary: Lower front teeth sit ahead of upper front teeth in the horizontal relationship.
review: Distinguish dental position from skeletal pattern
cases.limits: Reverse overjet does not by itself establish skeletal Class III or prove that surgery is needed.

quiz.question: What can reverse overjet alone establish?
quiz.explanation: The visible front-tooth relationship is descriptive; its cause requires broader assessment.

cases.name: Increased overjet
cases.summary: The upper front teeth project farther ahead of the lower front teeth horizontally.
review: Measure clinically with a documented method
Assess lips, function, and jaw relationships
cases.limits: Photo perspective changes apparent projection; no millimetre measurement is inferred here.

quiz.question: Overjet is the same measurement as overbite.
quiz.explanation: Overjet describes horizontal projection, whereas overbite describes vertical overlap.

cases.name: Anterior crossbite
cases.summary: One or more upper front teeth bite behind their lower counterparts.
review: Check for a functional bite shift
cases.limits: A localized crossbite is not automatically a skeletal underbite.

quiz.question: Does one upper incisor biting behind a lower incisor prove skeletal Class III?
options: Only if a photo is sharp
No; dental and functional factors need assessment
quiz.explanation: A single-tooth crossbite can reflect dental positioning; skeletal classification requires further records.

cases.name: Unilateral posterior crossbite
cases.summary: Upper back teeth bite inside lower back teeth on one side.
recognition: Reversed posterior relationship on one side
Watch closure for a sideways shift
review: Assess arch widths and tooth inclinations
cases.limits: A one-sided appearance can accompany a functional shift; one still image cannot resolve it.

quiz.question: Which additional observation is especially helpful?
quiz.explanation: Watching closure helps the clinician identify a functional mandibular shift.

cases.name: Bilateral posterior crossbite
cases.summary: Upper back teeth bite inside the lower teeth on both sides.
cases.limits: Both sides need usable records; no expansion amount is determined from a photo.

quiz.question: Bilateral means the finding affects which regions?
quiz.explanation: Bilateral posterior crossbite describes posterior involvement on both sides, subject to clinical confirmation.

cases.name: Scissor bite
cases.summary: Upper posterior teeth lie wholly outside their lower counterparts, disrupting normal interlocking contacts.
recognition: May affect one or both sides
review: Assess arch width and tooth inclinations
cases.limits: This is a distinct transverse pattern; the diagram does not determine an appliance or force system.

quiz.question: Which description best fits a scissor bite?
options: Upper back teeth entirely outside opposing teeth
quiz.explanation: Scissor bite describes a posterior transverse relationship with abnormal or absent interlocking contacts.

cases.name: Class II division 1
cases.summary: A Class II incisor relationship is accompanied by prominent upper incisors and increased overjet.
review: Review injury history and lip function
cases.limits: Dental classification is not skeletal classification; a frontal selfie is insufficient.

quiz.question: What distinguishes division 1 from division 2 in this teaching comparison?
quiz.explanation: Upper-incisor prominence contrasts with the retroclination typical of division 2.

cases.name: Class II division 2
cases.summary: A Class II incisor relationship includes inward-tilted upper central incisors, often with a deep bite.
cases.limits: A deep bite alone does not establish division 2 or select its management.

quiz.question: Which inclination is characteristic of upper central incisors in division 2?
quiz.explanation: Retroclined upper central incisors are characteristic, frequently accompanied by increased vertical overlap.

cases.name: Class III dental relationship
cases.summary: The lower dental relationship is positioned ahead of the upper; causes may be dental, skeletal, or functional.
recognition: Observe any forward shift on closure
review: Distinguish functional shift from skeletal pattern
cases.limits: Class III dental and skeletal labels are not interchangeable, and front-tooth appearance alone is insufficient.

quiz.question: A Class III dental relationship always proves which finding?
quiz.explanation: Dental, skeletal, and functional contributions require separate assessment.

cases.name: Dental midline discrepancy
cases.summary: Upper and lower dental centre lines do not coincide, or differ from the facial reference.
cases.limits: A tilted image can mimic discrepancy; dental and facial midlines must be distinguished.

quiz.question: What can create a misleading midline comparison?
quiz.explanation: Standardized orientation helps avoid confusing photographic distortion with dental displacement.

cases.name: Rotated teeth
cases.summary: A tooth is turned around its long axis relative to the arch.
cases.limits: Crown orientation does not reveal root anatomy or a safe movement path.

quiz.question: Which statement about rotation is appropriate?
options: It describes orientation, not a treatment plan
quiz.explanation: A visible rotation is an alignment observation; movement planning requires complete records.

cases.name: Suspected impacted canine
cases.summary: A permanent canine has not erupted as expected and needs localization by a clinician.
recognition: Canine absent from the visible arch
review: Assess adjacent teeth and available space
cases.limits: An unseen canine may be unerupted, absent, or impacted; a surface photo cannot distinguish these.

quiz.question: Can a smile photo locate an unerupted canine root?
quiz.explanation: Impaction assessment needs clinical examination and appropriately justified imaging, not a photo-derived root estimate.

cases.name: Absent tooth / possible hypodontia
cases.summary: A tooth is absent from the visible arch; the reason must be established.
recognition: Check whether a primary tooth remains
Confirm the dental and extraction history
review: Distinguish congenital absence from tooth loss
cases.limits: Hypodontia means developmental absence; a visible gap alone cannot establish it.

quiz.question: An empty tooth position proves congenital absence.
options: False; other explanations must be checked
True if the gap is small
quiz.explanation: Extraction, delayed eruption, impaction, and developmental absence require different assessments.

cases.name: Suspected supernumerary tooth
cases.summary: An additional tooth may be present beyond the expected dentition.
recognition: An extra crown may be visible
review: Chart primary and permanent teeth separately
cases.limits: A photo cannot exclude hidden additional teeth or establish removal as the best option.

quiz.question: Can a surface photo exclude all supernumerary teeth?
options: Yes, if all front teeth show
No; some additional teeth are unerupted
quiz.explanation: Clinical assessment may reveal teeth below the surface that are invisible in photographs.

cases.name: Ectopic eruption
cases.summary: A developing tooth follows an abnormal eruption position or path.
recognition: A tooth emerges outside the arch
review: Review eruption history and dentition stage
Assess nearby teeth and available space
Determine whether additional records are indicated
cases.limits: Abnormal position does not reveal its cause, hidden damage, or the required intervention.

quiz.question: What does ectopic eruption describe?
options: An abnormal eruption path or position
quiz.explanation: Ectopic eruption concerns how or where a tooth develops into the mouth.

cases.name: Mixed dentition review
cases.summary: Primary and permanent teeth coexist while the dental arches develop.
recognition: Both primary and permanent teeth present
cases.limits: The permanent 32-tooth atlas is not a patient-specific mixed-dentition reconstruction.

quiz.question: How should a permanent-tooth teaching atlas be used for a child?
options: As a reference, with the actual dentition charted
As proof all adult teeth are present
quiz.explanation: Developing dentition differs from a complete permanent-tooth reference model.

cases.name: Alignment change after treatment
cases.summary: Teeth can change position after orthodontic treatment; retention and review remain relevant.
recognition: A gap or rotation may reappear
review: Review previous treatment and retention history
Check retainer fit with the treating team
Assess current teeth and gum health
cases.limits: A single current image cannot establish when or why movement occurred.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of orthodontic retention?
quiz.explanation: Retainers help limit unwanted positional change; fit and ongoing care need professional review.

cases.name: Tooth wear and bite review
cases.summary: Loss of tooth surface may alter crown form and requires assessment of multiple possible causes.
review: Discuss dietary acid, reflux, and grinding history
Assess the pattern and progression clinically
cases.limits: Wear appearance alone does not diagnose grinding or establish that the bite caused the wear.

quiz.question: Visible tooth wear proves sleep grinding.
quiz.explanation: Acid exposure, tooth contact, and other factors can contribute; history and examination matter.

cases.name: Increased gingival display
cases.summary: More gum is visible above the upper teeth during smiling.
recognition: Record apparent crown and gum proportions
review: Ask about the patient's own concerns
Assess gum health and tooth exposure
cases.limits: Gum display is not automatically disease; a smile photo cannot identify its cause or appropriate management.

quiz.question: Does increased gum display automatically require treatment?
options: No; assess health, cause, and patient preferences
quiz.explanation: Appearance alone does not establish pathology or a need for intervention.

cases.name: Dental / facial asymmetry review
cases.summary: The arches, smile, or jaw position differ between sides and need comparison.
recognition: Compare right and left dental relationships
Check dental midlines and smile orientation
review: Distinguish dental, functional, and skeletal factors
cases.limits: One image cannot distinguish true asymmetry from camera distortion or establish skeletal diagnosis.

quiz.question: What is the appropriate first interpretation of apparent asymmetry in a selfie?
options: A finding to verify with standardized records
quiz.explanation: Orientation, clinical movement, and full dental records are needed to interpret an apparent side difference.
